page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine belonging to the g2 server family. It features an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 2 threads per core running at 2.2 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a 38 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and does not include local storage.

Acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, featuring 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in large language model inference tasks, achieving 11,784.81 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model and 2,225.82 tokens per second on a medium 7B model. Conversely, standard CPU-bound tasks show weaker performance, with single-core and multi-core Geekbench and stress-ng metrics falling into the bottom 25% and middle 50% categories.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the g2-standard-8 is highly optimized for workloads that can leverage GPU acceleration, particularly AI inference and machine learning tasks, where the NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers high resource density. However, for general-purpose CPU-only workloads, the lower single-core performance represents a tradeoff. This server is best suited for small to medium LLM inference, graphics rendering, and GPU-accelerated data processing pipelines, rather than heavy CPU-bound compilation or database operations.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for workloads requiring dedicated graphics hardware. It features an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, 32.0 GB of system memory, and a single NVIDIA L4 GPU with 24 GB of VRAM. While CPU-bound benchmarks place the instance in the average to weak performance tiers, its GPU-driven capabilities deliver top-tier results in large language model inference, processing over 2,200 tokens per second on medium 7B models. The server lacks local storage, relying on network-attached storage options. It is highly cost-efficient for AI inference, machine learning, and graphics rendering workloads, though it presents a tradeoff for CPU-intensive tasks.
